summary: POC scoping for a 2-week pilot to validate Marigold's chat-to-checkout flow at peak bursts. Main objectives: define workload cartography (QPS, concurrency, input/output token distributions), agree on success criteria (p95/p99 latency SLAs, throughput), collect sample traffic, and run benchmark runs in Redwood hosted and dedicated sims. Customer emphasized security (SOC2, VPC options), pricing sensitivity, and desire for clear rollback/fallback policy.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Marigold), Maya Ruiz (Marigold), Samir Patel (Marigold), Olivia Chen (Marigold)

Summary: quick kickoff to map traffic topology for the checkout chat assistant pilot, collect telemetry and agree success criteria.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan from redwood, and with me is priya. quick round?
[00:10] Ethan: ethan here, i'm head of platform at marigold, we've got maya on ml eng, samir sre and olivia product. thanks.
[00:18] Jordan: awesome. objective today - scoping the poc: workload shape, qps, concurrency, token mix, and what success looks like. probably 45 minutes of tech, last 10 for next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Olivia: yes, that's perfect. we want the pilot to prove we can handle peak checkout bursts with sub-200ms p95 on short prompts and fallback safely.
[00:36] Priya: clarifying — when you say peak checkout bursts, magnitude? qps or concurrent sessions?
[00:42] Maya: typical baseline is 8 qps, but during campaigns we've seen spikes up to ~180 qps sustained for 2-5 minutes; concurrency per model instance maybe 400 sessions, user sessions open and idle with KV cache warm.
[00:56] Jordan: ok that's useful, 8 steady, 180 spikes. what's the request/response token distribution look like?
[01:04] Maya: inputs are small, 20-40 tokens usually, but we have some follow-ups where output is 150-400 tokens for recommendation explanations. mean output ~120 tokens. there's also rerank calls that are pure short embeddings.
[01:19] Samir: also worth noting we have a subset of requests that use context windows ~2k tokens when we include history; that's maybe 5% of calls.
[01:28] Priya: great, that skew matters for kv cache pressure and memory; for benchmarking we need separate profiles: short-chat (70%), long-form context (5%), rerank/embedding (25%). does that split sound right?
[01:42] Maya: roughly yes, maybe rerank is 20, short-chat 75, long-form 5.
[01:48] Jordan: noted. success criteria — olivia mentioned p95 target, can you be explicit?
[01:54] Olivia: product wants p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500ms for the short-chat path at production concurrency; for long-form we accept higher p95 up to 1.2s. throughput target is to sustain steady 8 qps and survive the 180 qps bursts without dropping requests; acceptable queuing as long as 99.9% requests succeed.
[02:12] Ethan: also, cost per token is important; we have a threshold to keep inference cost below $0.0006 / token equivalent. that's negotiable but a baseline.
[02:23] Priya: understood. for the POC we'll run two bench modes: hosted-sim (Redwood hosted profile) and dedicated-sim (reserved capacity) to compare latency and unit cost. we'll also test fallback policy — routing to a smaller model on saturation.
[02:38] Jordan: quick question on data residency — do you need a private deployment?
[02:43] Samir: for pilot, hosted is ok but must pass SOC2 and log redaction; if it moves to prod we need VPC + KMS.
[02:51] Jordan: good, we'll include SOC2 docs and the network diagram.
[02:55] 
[03:05] --- Benchmark details ---
[03:05] Priya: here's the plan i sketched: 1) ingestion: provide 48h traffic CSV with timestamps, session ids, prompt text, token counts; 2) we run a traffic replay tool with configurable qps/concurrency and token mix; 3) collect p50/p95/p99, token throughput, GPU util, memory, and KV cache hit rates. we need target SLAs baked into the runner.
[03:30] Maya: can you share the csv schema? we have internal anonymization we run first.
[03:34] Jordan: yes, i'll send the template after the call.
[03:36] Priya: for load shapes we want to run: baseline steady 8 qps for 30 min, burst ramp to 180 qps for 5 mins, and a stress ramp to 300 qps for 1 minute to see graceful degradation. also a mixed-mode run with 25% rerank calls at 40 qps.
[03:53] Samir: for the caching bit — does redwood support prefix kv caching per customer session?
[03:58] Priya: yep, we can simulate prefix caching warm/empty states; caching reduces compute by reusing kv across recompletions. we'll report cache hit ratio impact on latency.
[04:08] Ethan: what's the expected GPU footprint for the 180 qps burst? we need a ballpark for budget and rack space planning if dedicated.
[04:16] Priya: rough initial sketch: depends heavily on model size and quantization. for a 13B int8 optimized model, 180 qps short-chat with batching might need ~6-8 GPUs in dedicated; with more quantization and smaller model variants you can get lower. we'll produce a capacity sketch in the follow up.
[04:33] Jordan: we should also capture tail-latency causes — queuing vs kernel saturation vs kv cache cold start. priya will instrument traces.
[04:40] Priya: correct. we will surface per-token latency breakdown and per-stage timings.
[04:45] 
[04:55] --- Security & compliance ---
[04:55] Samir: SOC2 is non-negotiable for prod. for pilot we need attestations and our security team will run a quick questionnaire. also, we prefer TLS egress disabled, prefer VPC peering or private link for later phases.
[05:08] Jordan: we'll attach SOC2 report and the network topology; we also provide an SSO integration guide for SAML.
[05:14] Maya: can redwood sign an addendum about not ingesting raw logs? we have PII concerns.
[05:19] Jordan: yes, we can provide log redaction and a data processing addendum.
[05:23] Olivia: timeline — we want POC results in three weeks, is that doable? two-week pilot plus analysis week?
[05:30] Priya: two weeks of runs plus a week of analysis is realistic; schedule depends on when we get the traffic sample. if we get the sample by 7/28 we can aim for analysis completed by 8/14.
[05:41] Ethan: budget decision cycles end 8/10 so that fits.
[05:44] 
[05:50] --- Objections / tradeoffs ---
[05:50] Ethan: cost sensitivity — if you route to smaller models for burst, we need to evaluate quality regression. we have automated evals for checkout correctness.
[06:00] Priya: we'll run A/B quality checks and instrument metrics for hallucination/regression against your eval set. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization or smaller variants that maintain quality.
[06:09] Olivia: also concerned about simultaneous rerank embedding traffic spiking during campaigns — we need a plan to deprioritize non-critical calls.
[06:18] Jordan: we can configure routing policies to throttle or queue rerank requests under capacity strain. that's part of the SLO gating.
[06:25] 
[06:30] --- Recap & Next steps ---
[06:30] Jordan: recap — we will: share csv schema and benchmark plan (jordan), redwood to run hosted-sim and dedicated-sim with the specified load shapes (priya), marigold to share 48h anonymized traffic and eval set (maya), security docs will be shared (jordan). aim for pilot start first week of august pending sample.
[06:49] Maya: we'll target sending the sample by 7/28 and confirm the test window.
[06:54] Samir: i'll check network constraints and raise any egress issues by 7/27.
[06:58] Jordan: excellent. we'll also include a cost projection and capacity sketch in the deliverables. any other questions?
[07:05] Olivia: no, that's good. thanks everyone.
[07:08] Jordan: thanks, call ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler removed. Misspellings present (e.g., kv cache spelled as k v cache in some places).
